headline: 1929 takes January.
deck: A debut book on top, two ties underneath, and both of them settled by head-to-head.
intro: Nine of you ranked ten candidates this round. 1929 (Sorkin) took it on 65 points, three clear of Something Rich and Strange, in its first appearance on a ballot, and reads January.
outcome: Winner: 1929 (65)   ·   Runner-up: Something Rich and Strange (62)   ·   Relegated: none — ten candidates, no relegation line
tieIntro: Two pairs finished level: The Black Count and Easy Money on 47, and Born to Run and The Eureka Machine on 40. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head first: ignore the rest of the ballot and ask how each voter ranked the two against one another.
tieVerdict: Both pairs separated cleanly. The Black Count beat Easy Money 5–4 and takes the higher of the two fifth places, and Born to Run beat The Eureka Machine 6–3 and takes the higher of the two ninth places. No fall-through to first-place votes was needed.
notes: A debut winner. 1929 had never been polled before and went straight to the top, with one first-place vote.
Something Rich and Strange led the field with two first-place votes, tied with Say Nothing, and finished second.
The River of Doubt reaches twenty-three polls and finished eighth on 44 points.
